author: The Stacks Project Authors

difficulty_reason: For a ring A, an adequate functor F and a flat ring map B -> B', the lemma asserts that F(B) tensor_B B' -> F(B') is an isomorphism (statement lines 441-447). The proof chooses the exact sequence 0 -> F -> M-underlined -> N-underlined presenting F as a kernel, applies the functor - tensor_B B' to obtain the displayed two-row diagram with exact rows (the top row because B -> B' is flat), observes that the right two vertical arrows are the canonical isomorphisms for module-valued functors, and concludes by the five lemma that the left arrow is an isomorphism (proof lines 449-464). The level is H2 under the current reading: the proof is short but contains a displayed diagram and a named substitution, so a reader can check the argument step by step.
